message.reasoning_content:
Key suspicion: the sequency ordering permutation. The standard mapping: sequency-ordered Walsh row k corresponds to Gray code of k... The natural-order butterfly computes H_N[row, x] with row = bit-reversed... Actually the fast Hadamard transform in natural order gives rows indexed by bit pattern; sequency order row k corresponds to reversed Gray code. Kernel: coefficient k -> source_lane = bitreverse(k) ^ (bitreverse(k)>>1) — that's Gray code of bit-reversed k. Need to verify empirically vs reference. Also int32 overflow within butterflies? Values are int16 inputs, butterfly sums bounded by N*32768 fits int32 fine. Just run a probe comparing run vs reference over sizes and batches including full-range values.

Record claim, run probe.
